findings.finding: MATH-0137 (Agoh-Giuga) states a WRONG equivalence and its falsification_criterion misfires on four mundane integers inside its own search range. The spec says a composite Giuga number 'requires all p|n satisfy p^2 does not divide n and p | n/p - 1' and declares any composite n<=1e7 passing this a counterexample to Giuga's conjecture. That is the definition of a Giuga NUMBER, not of an Agoh-Giuga counterexample; the Korselt half (p-1 | n/p - 1) is missing. Giuga numbers exist and are not counterexamples.
findings.evidence: Executed the spec's literal condition over all composite n<=1e7 (smallest-prime-factor sieve): hits = [30, 858, 1722, 66198]. For each I then computed the ACTUAL Agoh-Giuga statistic sum_{k=1}^{n-1} k^(n-1) mod n: n=30 -> 15 (needs 29); n=858 -> 429 (needs 857); n=1722 -> 861 (needs 1721); n=66198 -> 33099 (needs 66197). All four FAIL Agoh-Giuga; all four also fail the omitted Korselt condition. The spec would raise a counterexample alarm at n=30, the 30th integer it examines.
findings.required_fix: Add the Korselt condition: a composite n satisfies Agoh-Giuga iff for every p|n, p^2 does not divide n AND p | (n/p - 1) AND (p-1) | (n/p - 1). Restate the falsification_criterion against the conjunction.

findings.finding: MATH-0066 (Polignac) compares CONSECUTIVE-prime-gap counts N_2k against the Hardy-Littlewood singular series for prime PAIRS differing by 2k. These are different quantities and diverge fast in 2k, so the spec's '>20% deviation for small k' criterion fires on a well-understood distinction rather than on anything about Polignac.
findings.evidence: Sieve to 1e8. Observed N_2k/N_2 vs singular series prod_{odd p|k}(p-1)/(p-2): gap 6 -12.7%, gap 8 -24.1% (already outside the spec's 20% band at k=4), gap 12 -38.9%, and by gap 100 the deviation is -99.9% (N=878, obs ratio 0.0020 vs HL 1.3333). 47 of 50 rows exceed the spec's own 20% tolerance. The other half of the criterion is clean: no 2k<=100 has N_2k(1e8)=0 (gap 100 occurs 878 times below 1e8).
findings.required_fix: Either count prime PAIRS (p, p+2k) rather than consecutive gaps, or replace the HL pair prediction with a consecutive-gap model that includes the probability of no intervening prime. Keep the N_2k>0 sub-test, which is sound.

findings.finding: MATH-0065 (Cramer) inverts the direction of evidence AND, as written with no small-p cutoff, exceeds its own challenge threshold at p=2. Granville's refinement PREDICTS limsup g/ln^2 p >= 2e^-gamma = 1.1229; the spec treats ratios above ~1.2 as a CHALLENGE to the Granville frame when they would be its confirmation and Cramer's refutation.
findings.evidence: Executed the spec as written over primes to 1e8: max g(p)/ln^2(p) = 2.0814 at p=2 (gap 1), which trips the spec's own ~1.2 threshold on the trivial first gap. With a p>=100 cutoff the answer is stable at 0.7395 (p=20831323, gap 210); max gap in range is 220 after p=47326693. Constant check: 2e^-gamma = 1.12292.
findings.required_fix: State a small-p cutoff (p>=1e4 suffices; the value is cutoff-stable from 100 upward), and re-word the reading so ratios above 1.1229 register as SUPPORTIVE of the Granville frame and against Cramer's limsup=1.

findings.finding: MATH-0058 (twin) picks a normalization that guarantees a permanently unresolved reading. c_eff = pi_2(x) ln^2 x / x converges to 2C2 far too slowly to certify anything at 1e8, while the standard li_2 form resolves to four digits on the same data.
findings.evidence: Sieve to 1e8. c_eff by decade: 1e4 1.7390, 1e5 1.6224, 1e6 1.5592, 1e7 1.5323, 1e8 1.4941 vs target 2C2 = 1.3203 -- still 13.2% high after five decades, monotonically decreasing. Same counts against 2C2*li_2(x): obs/pred = 0.9904 (1e6), 1.0038 (1e7), 0.9999 (1e8). The falsification_criterion (monotone divergence over >=3 decades) will never fire, but neither will convergence ever be demonstrable.
findings.required_fix: Compare pi_2(x) to 2C2*li_2(x) = 2C2*integral_2^x dt/ln^2 t and keep c_eff only as a secondary display.

findings.finding: MATH-0129 (minimum overlap) has an unfalsifiable criterion: every n in its stated range lands outside the published bracket, and the escape clause is unquantified.
findings.evidence: Computed M(n) exactly for n<=12 by exhaustive partition search (fixing 1 in A to kill the A/B symmetry; M_k taken per-direction): 1,1,2,2,3,3,3,4,4,5,5,5. M(12)/12 = 0.4167 vs the spec's bracket [0.3809,0.3831] -- outside for every n<=12, though trending correctly toward it. The criterion 'outside the published bracket by a margin inconsistent with finite-n corrections' names no finite-n correction model, so any outcome is defensible either way. Separately the bracket's upper end is stale: Haugland's computation puts the constant near 0.380927 rather than leaving an open bracket to 0.3831.
findings.required_fix: Either state a finite-n correction form (e.g. fit M(n)/n = C + a/n and test the fitted C against the bracket) or reduce the spec to 'report the approach curve', which is honest and still certifies the harness.

findings.finding: MATH-0154 (EFL) overclaims its discovery value. The spec justifies itself as attacking 'the small-n regime where the asymptotic proof is silent', but small n for EFL is classically verified; the regime KKKMO leaves open is the MIDDLE range, not the small one. The spec is a calibration wearing an attack's framing.
findings.evidence: The spec's own published_bound field concedes it: 'EFL proven for all sufficiently large n (KKKMO 2021); small n classically checked'. A test whose target regime is already classically checked cannot be where a proof is silent. Additionally the data_source is under-specified: 'enumerate up to isomorphism OR randomized generation with certification' -- randomized generation cannot certify the absence of an (n+1)-chromatic configuration, so the two alternatives have different logical force and only the first supports the stated criterion.
findings.required_fix: Relabel as CALIBRATION alongside MATH-0212/0211, and pick one generation method; if randomized, restate the criterion as one-sided.

findings.finding: The TOOLS-DISCRIMINATE reading rests on a single tool that the same pass records as NONDETERMINISTIC. Firing a pre-stated discriminate reading on an outlier whose score is not even reproducible within the pass is a category error: the pre-stated trigger ('acc IQR >= 0.15 or structured surface spread') was met arithmetically, but the IQR was carried by a measurement the instrument could not repeat.
findings.evidence: P27 evidence lists the 0.75 top tool (Abductive_Reasoning---Adaptive_Control---Pragmatics) as NONdeterministic in the same line that names it. The determinism check itself is one probe called twice (the pass's own weakness 1). The binomial argument is sound in isolation -- I re-derived P(X>=15|Bin(20,0.25)) = 3.81e-06, Bonferroni over 46 = 2.0e-04, expected count 0.00018 -- but a p-value on an unreproducible score measures the draw, not the tool.
findings.required_fix: Gate the discriminate reading on determinism: a nondeterministic tool's accuracy must be averaged over repeats before it can carry a pre-stated reading, or excluded from the spread statistic.

findings.finding: The signature-existence probe was run at the wrong granularity for MATH-0060. The pass proved the COLUMN exists and is queryable; it never asked how much data the column holds. The zeta row stores 30 zeros. A Montgomery pair-correlation test against the GUE curve cannot be done with 30 zeros, and the spec's own published_bound invokes Odlyzko's agreement at height 1e20 as its benchmark.
findings.evidence: Queried the mirror directly: label '1-1-1.1-r0-0-0' fetches in 1.23s (the P49 index works) and its positive_zeros field parses to exactly 30 values, 14.134725 through 101.317851. That gives 435 total pairs, of which 71 fall within 3 mean spacings -- spread over a 12-bin pair-correlation histogram, about 6 pairs per bin. I ran the power check rather than asserting: 30 unfolded zeros DO detect level repulsion (0 of 4000 uniform-Poisson samples of the same size and span fit the GUE curve as well as the real zeros), so the test is not vacuous -- but detecting repulsion is not resolving the pair-correlation curve, and 'deviating from GUE beyond finite-size corrections' is not measurable at this n. The doctrine the pass invoked (signature-existence-first) is exactly the one that catches this: presence of a column is not sufficiency of its contents.
findings.required_fix: Add a CARDINALITY step to the probe protocol: record rows AND values-per-row, and state the minimum sample the statistic needs before the spec is filed. findings.finding: The artifact's residual is QUADRATURE ERROR, not mathematics. It reports obs/(C2*sg*J) 'flat at 0.994-0.995' and attributes the -0.5% to 'finite-size (small-prime edge terms), shrinking slowly'. The template's trapezoid over-integrates J(n) by almost exactly that amount, and the bias GROWS with n rather than shrinking. This is a numerical artifact given a number-theoretic explanation -- the narrative-resistance failure the pattern book exists to catch.
findings.evidence: hl_integral() uses np.linspace(2, n/2, 2000) -- a uniform-in-t grid whose first interval is ~25000 wide at n=1e8, straddling the region where 1/(ln t) moves fastest. Measured against scipy.quad at epsrel 1e-12, the template's J(n) is high by +0.005% (1e3), +0.059% (1e4), +0.206% (1e5), +0.341% (1e6), +0.447% (1e7), +0.541% (1e8). Monotonically INCREASING, while the artifact says the residual is 'shrinking slowly'.

findings.finding: The headline stability claim is manufactured by two errors moving in opposite directions, and correcting them makes the result STRONGER than published. findings.finding: INSTRUMENT_VALIDATED is issued at strength 'certain' on a validation that never probed T3 anywhere near its threshold, and the probe accepts a family carrying an 86 percent accurate unintended shallow composition. The rule the pass itself adopts - a probe that has never failed a known-negative cannot issue PASS - is satisfied only at the extreme: the single alt-composition known-bad sits at decoy probability 1.0. Between the clean null and that extreme lies a band the calibration never entered, and inside it the census returns FAMILY_ADMISSIBLE on genuinely leaky families.
findings.evidence: I ran the arm A1 omitted: a decoy-strength sweep in the calibration's own configuration (n=800, 8 fair independent bits, XOR target, seed 4242). decoy p=0.4 -> the unintended pair q05 XOR q06 predicts the label at 0.7300 accuracy, census best_alt 0.6112, verdict FAMILY_ADMISSIBLE. p=0.5 -> true pair 0.7875, best_alt 0.6637, ADMISSIBLE. p=0.7 -> true pair 0.8625, best_alt 0.6750, T1/T2/T3 all pass, ADMISSIBLE. Only at p=0.8 (true pair 0.9012, best_alt 0.7087) does T3 fire. A1's KNOWN_BAD_alt_composition was p=1.0 at best_alt 0.7612. The interventional sweep moved the MARGINAL leak only, so T3's sensitivity was never measured.
findings.required_fix: Run the decoy sweep as the second interventional arm and report the leak strength at which T3 first fires; then either set max_alt_acc from the clean-family null instead of by judgement, or state that FAMILY_ADMISSIBLE means 'no unintended pair above 0.70' rather than 'no unintended pair'. Until then INSTRUMENT_VALIDATED licenses FAIL verdicts and does not license PASS verdicts against alt-composition leakage.

findings.finding: The metamorphic consistency arm CANNOT FAIL. It is one of the three legs under INSTRUMENT_VALIDATED and it carries no discriminating power: the relation family is 'read bit k', the relabelling permutes data keys and target together, and the census never branches on a relation name - so every measured quantity is identical by construction rather than statistically close. It is computed on the SAME 800-row draw as the known-good fixture, which makes the identity exact rather than sampled.
findings.evidence: I recomputed the relabelling directly: worst marginal gap 0.0425 vs 0.0425, best alt accuracy 0.535 vs 0.535, occupancy fractions identical, the full multiset of marginal gaps identical. Only the name attached to the argmax moves (q02_ANDNOT_q07 -> q02_ANDNOT_q05). An invariance that succeeds proves equivariance and never capability (feedback_invariance_null_is_asymmetric); here it does not even prove that, since permutation-equivariance of dict-keyed code was never in doubt.
findings.required_fix: Either demote the arm to a code-hygiene check - it would catch a hardcoded 'q00' and nothing else - and stop counting it as one of three validation properties, or make it able to fail: permute the data without permuting the target, or use a relation family that is not permutation-symmetric.

findings.finding: The re-admissibility inference does not follow from the calibration, though its conclusion survives on grounds the pass did not state. A1 validated the probe on 8 independent fair bits at n=800 with an XOR target and one leak family; the three rejections were issued on graph worlds at n=400 with 9 non-independent relations. Validation on world A does not transfer authority to world B, and the pass asserts that transfer at strength 'certain'.
findings.evidence: I measured the missing null instead: 100 clean cell-balanced families at the rejections' own configuration (n=400, 9 independent relations, XOR target) give worst-marginal-gap median 0.0825, p95 0.1250, max 0.1550, and best-alt-accuracy median 0.5475, max 0.5800. World v2's decisive gaps (r06 0.255, r07 0.23) sit far above the clean maximum of 0.155, and its best alt (0.7175) far above the clean maximum of 0.58. The v2 rejection stands - because its own statistics exceed the clean-family null at its own n, not because a toy world later passed a calibration.
findings.required_fix: Restate claim 2 on the ground that carries it: a rejection is re-admissible when its statistics exceed the clean-family null AT ITS OWN n AND RELATION COUNT. Run that null once per rejected world - it costs seconds - and record the numbers beside the verdicts.

findings.finding: WEAKNESS MISSING, and it is one the loop's own pattern book names. T2 and T3 are ORDER STATISTICS - a max over 9 relation gaps, a max over 105 candidate shapes - compared against constants (0.15, 0.70) fixed independently of n, of relation count and of shape count. The false-rejection rate therefore moves with configuration while the numbers on the page stay still. The pass lists five weaknesses and this is not among them; weakness 3 says only that the calibration does not calibrate the thresholds.
findings.evidence: At n=400 with 9 relations a perfectly clean family already reaches worst-gap 0.155, past the 0.15 line, and T2 false-fails 1 clean family in 100. At n=800 with 8 relations the clean best_alt tops out near 0.58 against a 0.70 line - the same constant is tight in one test and loose by 0.12 in the other. aporia/catalog_attacks/ATTACK_PATTERNS.md section 3 carries ORDER-STATISTIC SCALING and ARGMAX-OF-NOISE as named patterns the loop applies to other people's data.
findings.required_fix: Derive both thresholds per-configuration from the clean-family null (clean max plus a stated margin), or keep the constants as policy and attach their measured clean false-fail rate at each configuration used.
